## What is C4?

The [C4 model](https://c4model.com/) describes a software system at four progressively zoomed-in levels:

| Level | Audience | What it shows |
|-------|----------|---------------|
| **1. Context** | Everyone | The system as a black box, its users, and external systems |
| **2. Container** | Tech-aware stakeholders | Deployable units (apps, services, databases) and their tech stacks |
| **3. Component** | Developers | Logical components inside a container and their relationships |
| **4. Code** | Developers maintaining the component | Classes/modules/functions inside a component |

Most teams only need **Context + Container** for day-to-day decisions. Component and Code levels are reference material — load them only when you need them.

## Cross-Layer Navigation

Every doc in this hierarchy links both DOWN (to its constituent layer) and UP (to the layer that contains it), so a reader can always traverse in either direction:

- **Code docs** (`code/c4-code-<dir>.md`) link to: their source files (`../../../<dir>/<file>#L<line>`), sibling code docs they depend on, and their **Parent Component** at the bottom.
- **Component docs** (`components/c4-component-<name>.md`) link DOWN to their constituent code docs and UP to their **Parent Container(s)** (libraries may have multiple).
- **Container docs** (`containers/c4-container-<name>.md`) link DOWN to deployed components, sideways to their IaC sources (`../../../docker-compose.yml#L<line>`, etc.), and UP to the **System Context**.
- The **AUTO-MANAGED** up-link blocks are populated by the c4-backlink agent at the end of every `/bmb:c4` run — do NOT hand-edit them.

## How to Use This Documentation

### From `/bmb:plan` or `/bmb:creative`
- For a Level 3-4 task, read `c4-context.md` and `c4-container.md` to ground the plan in the existing system shape.
- For a UI change, jump to `c4-container.md` to find which container hosts the affected components.
- For an algorithm or refactor, drill into the relevant `components/c4-component-<name>.md` and only then into `code/c4-code-<dir>.md`.

### From `/bmb:build`
- The TDD Agent reads `systemPatterns.md` § C4 Architecture (which links here) before exploring source.
- When introducing a new component (new custom addon), re-run `/bmb:c4 --scope custom_addons` so it is walked and indexed. To document an upstream addon your code extends, use `/bmb:c4 --scope addons/<name>`.
- When changing a deployment topology (new service, new datastore), `/bmb:c4 --refresh-from container` to regenerate Container + Context.

### From `/bmb:uat`
- Walker agents reference `c4-container.md` to identify which container's UI surface they're walking — useful for routing findings.

## Manifest

The [c4-manifest.md](./c4-manifest.md) tracks per-directory content hashes so reruns of `/bmb:c4` only re-walk subtrees that changed.

## Refresh Cadence

`/bmb:c4` is **idempotent**. Re-run it whenever:
- A new component, service, or container is introduced
- A deployment topology changes (split, merge, new datastore, new external integration)
- Before a major release that needs current architecture artifacts
- After significant refactors

It will skip subtrees whose source-directory hashes are unchanged.
